Remark
[special cases of the complex sectional curvature]

Source: petersen:page-0371 ↗ lem:pet-ch9-complex-sectional-curvature-real-formula Three specializations of the preceding formula are used:

  1. $y=v=0$ gives the ordinary sectional quantity $R(x,u,u,x)$;

  2. orthonormal $x,y,u,v$ gives the isotropic curvature;

  3. $u=v$ gives $2R(x,u,u,x)+2R(y,u,u,y)$, called the second Ricci curvature when $x,y,u$ are orthonormal.
